A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same NFL-BA work, with matching methods and identifiable shared experiments. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement; references to separate supplementary material cannot be verified.

before.justification: v2 reports original C3VD tracking, mapping, rendering and runtime results, plus qualitative Colon10K reconstructions.

after.justification: v3 retains original endoscopy results and adds quantitative indoor-scene evaluations and a static-versus-dynamic lighting comparison.

M1.justification: The albedo/shading rendering model, bundle-adjustment objective, zero angular attenuation and normal calculations remain equivalent. v3 newly documents gamma correction, but does not establish that this represents a procedural change rather than additional implementation disclosure.

E1.justification: v3 extends evaluation beyond C3VD and Colon10K to four self-captured nonmedical scenes: Guitars, Porch, Pool and Stairs. It also includes static and moving co-located illumination scenarios, substantially broadening the represented environments.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 compares NICE-SLAM with and without NFL-BA using PPSNet depth; that comparison is absent from v3's predicted-depth evaluation. NICE-SLAM remains in the oracle-depth comparison, while MonoGS and EndoGSLAM remain in both depth settings.

E3.justification: The added indoor evaluation introduces RGB-D capture with camera-mounted lighting, motion-capture reference trajectories, ATE measured in metres and LPIPS, without Chamfer evaluation because reference point clouds are unavailable. Figure 2 adds a static/dynamic lighting control. These are new evaluation protocols, not demonstrated reruns of the retained C3VD experiments.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 2 tests whether NFL-BA recovers performance lost under dynamic illumination. Conversely, v2's small control showing that EndoGSLAM depth rescaling alone changes baseline ATE from 3.03 to 3.38 mm is no longer reported. The image-formation validation and clinical case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither PDF reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty estimates. Trajectory plots describe tracking errors rather than run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Matched C3VD table values remain unchanged. v3 Table 3 adds four indoor comparisons, including Guitars ATE of 0.30 m for Photo-BA versus 0.18 m for NFL-BA. v3 omits the NICE-SLAM/PPSNet result rows, oracle-depth LPIPS entries and v2's detailed runtime results, substantially changing the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations remain equivalent: v2's rendering, shading and optimization equations are regrouped and renumbered in v3. Neither version introduces theorems or proofs, and the expanded explanations do not change the formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the contribution from improving endoscopic SLAM to SLAM under dynamic co-located lighting generally. v3 adds a claim of approximately 35% average indoor tracking improvement and motivates applications such as subterranean robotics and search-and-rescue.

C2.justification: v3 clarifies that the validation's HSV-derived albedo is only an approximation, discusses angular-attenuation calibration as future work, and interprets indoor results as evidence of broader applicability. It omits v2's explanation of NICE-SLAM's predicted-depth sensitivity. The limitations concerning specularity, subsurface scattering and inter-reflections remain.

D1.justification: v3 adds gamma values, the HSV albedo-estimation procedure, GPU information and dataset-processing details. However, numerical loss weights, EndoGSLAM depth rescaling, NICE-SLAM's bounding-box construction and albedo multiplier, and point-cloud alignment instructions are no longer supplied. Hyperparameters and runtime details are deferred to unavailable supplementary material; v2's project/results link also disappears.

R1.justification: v3 adds a Dynamic Lighting in SLAM discussion covering photometric calibration, unscented filtering and illumination-robust matching, with new references including LightGlue and AirSLAM. It shortens the deformable-surgery discussion and removes several associated references while retaining the main neural-rendering and near-field-lighting positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, background and method explanations undergo substantial rewriting. Evaluation changes from separate method-specific subsections to organization by dataset and depth setting; implementation material is redistributed and limitations move into the conclusion. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a single-column layout, redraws the overview, splits the main C3VD table, adds an indoor table and lighting/indoor figures, and combines MonoGS trajectory and reconstruction displays. Other figures are rearranged, and trajectory captions correct v2's reversed color descriptions.

improvement.justification: The new lighting control and four nonmedical scenes strengthen evidence for the method's mechanism and broader applicability. Albedo/gamma explanations and corrected figure captions also improve clarity. The net gain is limited because the supplied v3 omits mixed NICE-SLAM predicted-depth results and detailed runtime and implementation information, reducing completeness and reproducibility.
